It, however, does not state specific plans to attract more transit riders. The plan does implement Milwaukee County's freeway system by proposing a modified mass transportation system, using rubbertired express busses which would operate over the existing freeway system.
The Regional Land Use - Transportation Plans clearly established that a fixed rail rapid transit system would be inferior to the more flexible and economical bus rapid transit system and no further consideration would be given to other forms of rapid transit.
The successful "Freeway Flyer" operation has already demonstrated that a bus transit system will work in the Milwaukee urbanized area.
Milwaukee Area Transit Plan
Further refinement of the Milwaukee County Jurisdictional Highway Plan resulted in a study report entitled "Milwaukee Area Transit Plan", dated June 1971. This plan was adopted by SEWRPC on March 2, 1972 and the Milwaukee County Board on May 8, 1973.
The Airport Spur Freeway proposal is compatible with the Milwaukee Area Transit Plan in that the proposed south transit corridor of the North-South Freeway alignment serves four major industrial areas, three major service and retail areas as well as General Mitchell Field airport. It also recognizes the importance of co-ordinating long range air and ground transportation systems by providing airport service.
